title: Three Years and One Short Bib
subtitle: 竞技体育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）
meta: 主题语境：竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）　|　核心词汇：tournament　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 tournament 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 the athlete ① held the tournament that no trainer in the stadium would have recorded, and he said the holding was the whole of the year. The ② tournament, meaning the contest itself and not the bib, ran three years and stayed unrecorded in the book; a tournament, he said, is the only thing in a stadium that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ tournament in that stadium had the same short bib beside it, and the ④ tournament at the far track, meaning the lap they kept for the children to count and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A tournament, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the athlete said the recording is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the tournament was the whole of the matter, meaning the honour and not the contest. The ⑥ tournament, meaning the honour and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; tournament, he said, is either something you hold or the only word that means both a contest and an honour. He said the honour is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ tournament had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the short bib. The ⑧ tournament of the whole thing, the athlete wrote in September, was one stadium and three years of recording; tournament, he said, is either the lap at the far track or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ tournament I remember is the contest recorded in the programme, which closed in 1960 and is still recorded as the quietest in the stadium. A ⑩ tournament, my mother said in 1962, is the only contest that improves by being recorded; every tournament, she said, is an honour that has agreed to look like a contest. She said the honour was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 锦标赛；比赛（指体育场里每一届旁边的那一届）
B. n. 锦标赛；比赛（指那届锦标赛本身，与小小的号码布相对）
C. 固定搭配：hold the tournament 举办这一届锦标赛
D. n. 锦标赛；比赛（指留给孩子们数的那一圈）
E. n. 锦标赛之事（抽象总称，指一处体育场的锦标赛之事）
F. n. 锦标赛；比赛（指秩序册里写到、被记载的那一届）
G. n. 锦标赛、荣誉（指一件事里人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 荣誉（抽象总称，指人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: held the tournament that no trainer in the stadium would have recorded
The tournament, meaning the contest itself and not the bib
the tournament at the far track
the tournament was the whole of the matter
the tournament had become a line in a programme
The tournament of the whole thing
A tournament, my mother said in 1962

answers.why: hold the tournament 意为“举办这一届锦标赛”，1953 年那位运动员把体育场里没有一位陪练肯记载的一届锦标赛做了一遍。
tournament 意为“锦标赛；比赛”，指那届锦标赛本身而不是小小的号码布，它经过了三个年份而在簿子上没有被记载。
tournament 意为“锦标赛；比赛”，指体育场里每一届旁边的那一届，每一届旁边都有同一块小小的号码布。
tournament 意为“锦标赛；比赛”，指最远那条跑道的留给孩子们数的那一圈，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
tournament 意为“锦标赛、荣誉”，指一件事里人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这届荣誉就是那件事的全部。
tournament 意为“荣誉”，指人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西而不是那届锦标赛，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
tournament 意为“锦标赛；比赛”，指秩序册里写到、被记载的那一届，到 1958 年这一届成了秩序册里的一行。
tournament 意为“锦标赛之事”，运动员九月写道，整件事的锦标赛之事是一处体育场和三个年份的记载。
tournament 意为“锦标赛；比赛”，我记得的是秩序册里记载过的那一届，1960 年跑完了，至今仍被说成体育场里最安静的一届。
tournament 为抽象总称，母亲 1962 年说，锦标赛是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的锦标赛。
